synthesis:draft.headline: AEMO's POE50 pre-interval forecast for 2026-07-29 17:30 ACST was 1816.0 MW; actual operational demand was 1872.0 MW, so the forecast error (POE50 − actual) was −56.0 MW (−2.99%).
summary: Forecast POE50 for target_end_utc 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z (2026-07-29 17:30 ACST) was 1816.0 MW [ev0560].
Actual operational demand for that half-hour was 1872.0 MW [ev0561].
Forecast error (POE50 − actual) reported for that half-hour was −56.0 MW [ev0562], equal to −2.99% [ev0563].
Across the compared targets in the 2026-07-29T02:00:00Z—2026-07-29T14:00:00Z window, the run's mean absolute error (MAE) was 44.0 MW [ev0638].

possible_explanations.statement: The forecast might reflect a smaller step-up between the half-hours ending 2026-07-29T07:30:00Z and 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z than actually occurred, i.e. the actual increase between those intervals (ev0534 and ev0535) could have been larger than the run anticipated (ev0560).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare the actual half-hour operational demands for 2026-07-29T07:30:00Z and 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z (evidence ev0534 and ev0535) with the run's POE50 for those targets (the run's POE50 for 07:30 and 08:00 as given in forecast outputs); a larger-than-expected increase in the actuals versus the POE50 changes would support this explanation.

possible_explanations.statement: The run's residual error might reflect short-term, higher-frequency variations (within the half-hour) or data updates not captured in the half-hour POE50 (the run's POE50 ev0560 and the actual ev0561 may mask within-interval volatility).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain higher-resolution dispatch or metered demand (for example, five-minute TOTALDEMAND) for the 2026-07-29T07:30:00Z—2026-07-29T08:00:00Z window and compare the intra-half-hour pattern to the half-hour averages (if the five-minute series shows peaks that the half-hour average smooths, this would support the hypothesis).

possible_explanations.statement: A systematic bias in this run (the run's MAE was 44.0 MW [ev0638]) might mean similar-sized errors recurred across targets; the observed −56.0 MW error at 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z could be one instance of that pattern.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine the per-target errors across the window (the compare_forecast_actual 'pairs' entries) to see whether errors of similar sign and magnitude occur frequently; a consistent sign and magnitude would support a systematic bias explanation.
